symptom: With a global `url.git@github.com:.insteadOf https://github.com/` rule (a common developer setup), `mxcli git doctor` reports an HTTPS remote as `origin: git@github.com:org/app.git — SSH; Studio Pro needs HTTPS`, exits 1, and `--fix` "rewrites" the configured URL to HTTPS on every run (dropping its `.git` suffix) without changing anything git uses
cause: The remote check read `git remote get-url`, which applies url.<base>.insteadOf, and --fix set `remote.<name>.url`, which the rule rewrites again on the next read, so the check could never pass. The same read made the two SSH tests depend on the developer's and the sandbox's git config (ako/mxcli#1765 isolated the tests; the product question stayed open)
file: `cmd/mxcli/gitdoctor.go` (`doctorRun`: judge `git config --get remote.<name>.url`; report a differing `git remote get-url` as an [i] insteadOf line); tests `TestGitDoctor_InsteadOfRewriteIsNotAnSSHRemote`, `TestGitDoctor_ConfiguredSSHRemoteFoundBehindRewrite` in `cmd/mxcli/gitdoctor_test.go`
insight: **A check and its fix must read and write the same thing.** `remote get-url` is the effective URL, `remote set-url` writes the configured one; with a rewrite in between, a fix can never make its own check pass, and a loop like that is the tell. Judge what you can change (the configured URL) and report what you cannot (the rule, which applies to every git command on the machine). **Put the rule in the test repository's own config and use a host nobody rewrites** (git.example.com): the test then shows the behaviour without inheriting the developer's or the CI sandbox's rewrites of github.com, which point in opposite directions. Set GIT_SSH_COMMAND=false when the effective URL is SSH, or ls-remote reaches for the network
